mainText:
Good morning, it's Saturday, Nov. 28.

US military detonates aging lead explosives at Iowa facility.
Army officials said the controversial plan was needed as roughly 10,000 pounds of degraded lead azide—a volatile compound used in detonators—was at risk of spontaneously exploding. Measurements afterward showed minimal levels of lead in the air.
Rocker the coonhound wins National Dog Show.
The three-year-old black and tan became the first of his breed to take best in show in the event's history. (None had ever placed in the top four.) Rocker, who beat out runner-up Kissy the Lhasa Apso, is expected to compete in the Westminster Dog Show at the end of January.
Star QB Aaron Rodgers abruptly released by the Pittsburgh Steelers.
After being benched Tuesday amid a rift with Coach Mike McCarthy, the Super Bowl-winning quarterback gave a scorched-earth interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" (
watch here
). Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep during team meetings, among other issues—he was let go Wednesday afternoon.
Scientists develop nanorobots for drug delivery in the brain.
These tiny devices, hundreds of times smaller than the width of a human hair, are injected into the bloodstream and triggered via infrared light to cross the blood-brain barrier. The approach could one day be used to treat hard-to-reach conditions like glioblastoma.
Learn how the blood-brain barrier protects the brain but also makes it
challenging to treat diseases
(w/video).
Trump administration proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners.
Targets include China, Japan, and the European Union, and are said to address countries with artificially high production capacity in certain manufacturing sectors.
French actor Gérard Depardieu charged with rape.
The 77-year-old performer, who has starred in more than 200 films, is accused of raping then-22-year-old actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. Depardieu, who was separately convicted of sexually assaulting two women on set last year, has denied the charges.
